name: Florida

office.name: FDOT State Permit Office (Over-Weight Over-Dimension Permits)

fees.note: Overdimension trip permit (10 days) up to 12' W, 13'6" H, 85' L: $5. The tier is set by the largest dimension. Overlength semitrailer 53'-57'6" only: $10 (not modeled).

Overweight trip permit per FL mile: to 95,000 $0.27; 112,000 $0.32; 122,000 $0.36; 132,000 $0.38; 142,000 $0.42; 152,000 $0.45; 162,000 $0.47. Miles are billed in 25-mile increments rounded up, total rounded up to the dollar (not modeled). Overweight + dimension fee combined is capped at $500 (not modeled).
Over 162,000 lb: $0.003 per 1,000 lb per mile (= $0.006 per ton-mile of gross weight).
Administrative cost $3.33 for permits over 80,000 lb. A $5 transmission fee applies when applicable (not modeled).

escorts.when: Over 12' wide, on interstates and freeways
Over 12' wide, on two-lane and other roads
Over 150' long, on two-lane and other roads

police.when: Over 16' wide, on two-lane and other roads
police.text: 2 police escorts. Over 16' wide: two law enforcement escorts at all times on state roads other than limited access (local moves only); on limited access 1 LE + 1 qualified escort at night
1 police escort. Over 16' high: one law enforcement escort plus a qualified escort with height pole; local moves only; utility personnel at low wires/signals
1 police escort. Over 250' long: one law enforcement escort plus one qualified escort

restrictions.text: Overwidth: daytime only (1/2 hour before sunrise to 1/2 hour after sunset); up to 10' wide may move all days.

Over 10' wide: excluding weekends and holidays - FDOT's permit definition allows 1/2 hour before sunrise to noon on Sat/Sun; no travel on New Year's, Memorial Day, Independence Day, Labor Day, Thanksgiving and the day after, Christmas (Friday/Monday also observed when the holiday falls on a weekend).
Over 12' wide: no movement in congested areas during peak traffic hours unless authorized by permit; two escorts required on lanes under 12', bridges under 30' curb to curb, or high-ADT roads.
Over 16' wide: trip permits for local moves only, District Traffic Engineering review; over 22' wide needs a route horizontal-clearance affidavit.
Over 14'6" high: daytime only, excluding holidays; over 16' high local moves only; over 18' needs a route clearance affidavit (height + 6").
Over 80' long: daytime only, excluding holidays; over 85' no movement in congested areas during peak hours.
No travel when visibility is under 1,000 ft. Night moves only when recommended by the District Traffic office or required by the permit, and then with law enforcement escort(s).

travel.note: 14-26.012(7)(a): up to 10 ft wide moves all days, daytime only; holidays close only over 10 ft.

closures: sat, sun from 12:00: Over 10 ft wide: Saturday and Sunday from 1/2 hour before sunrise until noon only

notes: Legal: 102" wide (96" on lanes under 12'), 13'6" high, 53' semitrailer with kingpin up to 41' (40' single unit, 68' truck-trailer), 3' front overhang, 80,000 lb.
Loads up to 10' wide (or up to 14'6" high, or up to 80' long, with other dims legal) may move all days; the 10' daytime rule is for width.

Single escort for 12-14' wide: precedes on two-lane highways, follows on four-lane divided highways (modeled interstate = rear, non-interstate = front). Overlength-only escorts ride in the rear; over 150' needs two qualified escorts except one on limited access.
Self-issue trip permits in PAS go up to 16' W, 18' H, 150' L, 200,000 lb; the superload flag here marks loads beyond that envelope (FDOT has no formal 'superload' term).
Rule 14-26.012(5)(e) says movement is prohibited on weekends and holidays unless noted on the permit; FDOT's published definition allows weekend travel until noon. Verify current permit wording.
